Subject: Pilot load & success criteria — next steps and traffic intake

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can scope the pilot workload correctly. Please confirm or correct any numbers below.

Summary of the ask:
- Pilot goal: validate latency & cost targets for embedding + chat enrichment on a subset of 10k daily queries, with a final decision gate after two weeks of representative traffic.
- Success criteria (prelim): 95th perc latency < 350ms for text-generation path, embedding throughput >= 1500 reqs/min, and per-token cost within 20% of our initial estimate.

Traffic/workload intake (please confirm):
- Typical steady-state RPS: 8 req/s (embedding) and 2 req/s (generation) during business hours
- Peak/burst patterns: up to 45 req/s for short bursts (1–3 minutes) during batch ingest and morning syncs
- Average input token length: 120 tokens; 95th percentile token length: 640 tokens (occasional long clinical notes)
- Concurrent sessions: up to 30 simultaneous generation sessions from the web app during peak 09:00–11:00 PT
- KV cache hit expectation: ~30% for repeated patient-context prompts

Operational details / constraints:
- Data residency: US-only, no PHI should be stored in the hosted logs — Aster will need Private or Dedicated for any PHI. For this pilot Aster will send anonymized test traffic.
- Timeline: target pilot start Apr 6, 2-week run, decision meeting Apr 24

Next steps I propose:
1) Samir/Priya: confirm traffic numbers above and attach any sample logs or batch sizes (reply by Tue 3/30)
2) Connor: I'll loop you in for sizing and a suggested config (GPU type, instance counts)
3) I will upload a shared metrics sheet and a minimal test harness scaffold to the Drive folder (link below)

Attachments: I attached a blank pilot metrics template — please copy and populate the green cells and send back.

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu

Thanks Jasmine — confirming numbers with a few clarifications below. Apologies for the long email, wanted to be explicit so we avoid back-and-forth.

Confirmed numbers (we validated with infra):
- Steady-state: embedding 7.5 RPS (avg), generation 2.2 RPS (avg). We included a 10% buffer but those are the observed averages over our morning windows.
- Bursts: we see short 60–180s spikes to 40–50 RPS during morning batch reconciliation and daily sync with partner systems; these are rare but must not time out.
- Token lengths: median 95 tokens, mean ~140, 95p is ~610 tokens. We'll export a sample distribution.
- Concurrency: up to 32 simultaneous interactive sessions; back-end batch jobs will run in parallel but we can gate them during test windows if needed.

PHI note: for pilot we'll run an anonymized dataset. If we go to Dedicated/Private we will provide HIPA-compliant connectivity and KMS.

Attached: small network trace and a filled section of the pilot metrics sheet with real numbers from last week's window.

Proposed timeline tweak: can we shift start to Apr 8? Two of our engineers are OOO Apr 6–7. If Apr 8 works, we can still finish decision meeting Apr 24.

Thanks — Samir

Thanks for the details — great summary. Based on the numbers Samir confirmed, here's a proposed pilot config and ownership split: 

Sizing suggestion (initial):
- Dedicated pilot cluster: 2x A100-40GB (or equivalent A10G fallback) behind autoscaler tuned for latency SLOs
- Serving config: batch window 10ms, dynamic batching for embedding path up to 64 seqs; generation path batch size capped at 8 for interactive latency
- KV cache: local in-memory cache with warm-up preloads for the 2k most common patient contexts
- Network: allow brief burst headroom (scale-up policy aggressive, +30% within 60s) to cover 40–50 RPS spikes

Metrics we will collect (redwood console):
- Token-level latency (p50/p90/p95), per-model throughput, egress bytes, cache hit rate, and cost-per-1000-tokens
- Error profile and retry counts (especially for 500/503 during scale events)

Ownership / runbook:
- Redwood (Connor): cluster provisioning, runtime config, initial warmup, and dashboard setup; on-call for the pilot window
- Aster (Samir, Priya): provide anonymized traffic feed, approve maintenance windows for batch gates, and validate test queries as representative
- Redwood (Jasmine): coordinate checkpoints, decision meeting, and evaluation scoring

Next steps I will take today:
1) Create a draft resource config and post it to the Drive pilot folder
2) Pre-populate the console with baseline dashboards and synthetic warm-up job

If Samir/Priya are OK with Apr 8 start, I'll aim to have infra provisioned by Apr 6 so we can run smoke tests Apr 7.

Connor O'Brien
